title: Sleep vs Ticks Timeline
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Clocks and Watches with AI
description: Two timelines compare a blocking sleep(1) loop with a non-blocking ticks_diff() loop and measure how long each takes to notice a button press.

learningObjectives: Compare blocking timing with sleep() and non-blocking timing with ticks_ms() and ticks_diff()
Measure the delay (latency) before each program notices a button press
Explain why a program that sleeps cannot respond to input

accessibility.notes: Controls are standard HTML form elements; the canvas has a describe() text for screen readers

keyQuestions: What can the top program do while it is asleep?
Why is the bottom program never more than about 10 ms late?
Do both programs blink the LED at the same rate?
commonMisconceptions: A button press is stored until the program wakes up and is never late
sleep() lets other code run in the background
Non-blocking code makes the LED blink faster
assessmentOpportunities: Students state the longest possible delay for each program (about 1000 ms and about 10 ms).
Students explain the word "blocking" using the gray blocks.
Students identify which program to use for a stopwatch with a start button, and why.

controls.label: Start / Pause

controls.label: Press button
controls.description: Presses the button at the current simulated time

controls.label: Reset
